title: Maintain a live connection and synchronize remote editor changes locally
description: Implement a persistent subscription-driven Leaflet watch session over selected bound local documents. Reuse the single-document adoption/classification pipeline; maintain rootEntity poke subscriptions, initial catch-up, coalescing, reconnect and bounded slow reconciliation. Report connection health independently of per-file agreement. Probe separate Yjs presence as advisory activity evidence, with no assumption that no observed peers proves an idle document. Public realtime bootstrap/channel access needs source and deployment evidence. Polling-only does not fulfill the delivery.
design: design/keyed-build-path0.gpt6a.md#5-continuous-inbound-sync-is-an-early-deliverable — accepted connected watch direction, presence experiment and transport boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: A real persistent connection drives saved remote changes into supported clean local files; events during catch-up cause another pass; reconnect catches missed changes; local dirty/conflicted/invalid/pending files are preserved; repeat equal reads preserve bytes/mtime; local writers cooperate under locking; degraded subscription state is explicit. Synthetic socket/HTTP tests cover races and reconnect; bounded deployed connection proof establishes bootstrap/topic access. Presence probe records actual support and limits separately; peer count never controls write authority or disables quiet-document subscriptions.

title: Design a right-sized native edit strategy with independent cross-review
description: Design how Leafbud should enact local desired content in existing native Yrs text and the outer fact graph, including concise explanation of intended effects. Astra high and g independently assess existing tools/Yrs APIs, small identity-preserving wins, coarse block/page update strategies, recovery/read-back and modest extension seams. Structural optimization is secondary to bounded conceptual complexity for a low-volume product. No saved bases or CRDT snapshots are introduced. Diff is an incidental implementation aid rather than a general framework to build. Human display diff is a separate implementation ticket. Both authors commit independent drafts before reading each other; then each adds a cross-review with its revised stance. No production edit engine implementation in this task.

Determine whether the goal is a user-facing comparison adequately served by common CLI tools or a good library, structural comparison (a much more complex tool), or a justified combination. Future exploration, not commissioned implementation. Investigate an MDX-like declarative markup encoding for Leaflet documents that preserves rich blocks and unknown block types alongside ordinary Markdown. Treat JSON and markup as alternative encodings of one logical document, not synchronized source/output copies. Preserve document metadata and embedded @leafspring state through frontmatter or an equivalent declarative mechanism; never execute arbitrary embedded code to decode a document. Define round-trip fidelity tests and explicit loss reports. Plain Markdown down-conversion should require --force-downconvert when canonical content cannot be preserved. title: Support explicit PDS-managed pull, push, and conflict resolution
description: Future PDS-managed adapter for the document-centered architecture; the pre-reset sync implementation at revision 80436b61 is historical evidence; the current CLI implements native draft import/pull and has no PDS-managed synchronization workflow. Reuse the shared two-edge classifier and one-file @leafbud witnesses without storing base documents, sidecars, or a separately synchronized source file. Bind published identity to exact AT URI, never filename/path; use record CID preconditions for updates and report stale comparisons. Provide current-local/current-remote diff, explicit choose-local/choose-remote resolution, semantic fingerprints, post-write verification, and bounded interrupted-write recovery. Filename/path tidy remains independent. Preserve unknown record content and distinguish application-inflated content from actual PDS/offloaded payloads. Document that record updates can leave the Leaflet editor stale and a later native republish can overwrite them; management-mode changes must be explicit. Acceptance: coherent adapter design/implementation, offline classification and conditional-write tests, no accidental duplicate records after rename/path edit, no implicit deletion or cleanup, and public CLI documentation of lifecycle differences. title: Redesign explicit PDS-managed publishing with caller-selected record keys
description: Future alternative to the primary Leaflet-managed lifecycle; the pre-reset publish run implementation is historical recovery evidence at revision 80436b61, while the ATProto library remains retained; the current CLI has no implemented PDS publish workflow. Carry that capability into the document-centered redesign deliberately: consume the current managed MDX document through an explicit public-record projection and strip local @leafbud state from the wire output, choose/validate an initial rkey explicitly rather than deriving it from filename, persist actual AT URI as identity, preserve it on updates, and surface path/routing constraints. A document has one chosen management mode, never simultaneous independent Leaflet/PDS writers. Preview the identity and the native lifecycle differences (application/editor linkage, publish versioning, revalidation, newsletter/mention/share behavior); do not assume firehose ingestion reproduces every native side effect or silently substitute this path for failed native publication. Acceptance: design and implementation of the explicit PDS-managed first-publication path with offline transport tests, key collision/conditional-create behavior, envelope stripping, identity preservation, and precise lifecycle tradeoff documentation. No live writes without separate operator authorization. Origin: opencode://ses_e4900b8d7ffeDT9QuFwmKRAB7t, user-requested PDS alternative during redesign round 1.
